gaps.sentence: He lowered his voice ___ wake the baby.
gaps.explanation: Negative purpose = so as not to / in order not to + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: I'd rather cycle ___ wait twenty minutes for an unreliable bus.
gaps.explanation: 'Would rather... than...' is the fixed pattern for preferences.

gaps.sentence: He spends money ___ it grew on trees.
gaps.explanation: 'As if it grew on trees' — the unreal comparison justifies the criticism.

gaps.sentence: He had hardly stepped off the plane ___ he was rushed into a meeting.
___ the theory is elegant, the data simply don't support it.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though' grants the fact (the theory is elegant) before contradicting it.

gaps.sentence: The flat is spacious and well located; ___, the rent is surprisingly low.
gaps.explanation: 'Moreover' adds another supporting point in the same direction.

gaps.sentence: I'll take the job ___ they don't offer me any more money.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a future possibility that will not change the decision.

gaps.sentence: ___ the fact that costs had doubled, the project was allowed to continue.
gaps.explanation: 'Despite the fact that' = although, in a more formal wrapper.
